why: Count with a frequency map, then use buckets indexed by frequency: a frequency is between 1 and n, so bucket[f] lists the values seen f times and reading buckets from n downward yields the most frequent values without sorting all of them.
hints: First, how many times does each value appear? Then the question is only about those counts.
Counts are integers in 1..n. Instead of sorting values by count, make an array of n+1 lists and drop each value into bucket[count].

Walk f from n down to 1, appending bucket[f] (smaller values first, as the tie rule asks) until you have k values. O(n) plus sorting inside buckets for the tie order; a size-k heap is the O(n log k) alternative.
pitfalls: Return distinct values, not repeated occurrences.
Ties: equal-frequency values are listed smallest first.
The bucket array needs n+1 slots because a value can appear n times.
